item.content:encoded:
The Ukrainian-Russian battle of the flags. The offensive that never was

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-19

On 12 August, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine had recaptured 745 km² of territory and 26 settlements in a large-scale offensive operation conducted by the Air Assault Forces together with sub-units from other formations on the Oleksandrivka axis, at the junction of the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. The operation unfolded in two phases: from January to May and from May to August.

Zelensky’s statement, based on a report presented to him by the new Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, General Mykhailo Drapatyi, has drawn sharply divergent reactions from military observers and OSINT sources. Some have challenged the account, arguing that it relied on overinterpretation, manipulation or even outright falsehoods, while also viewing it as detrimental to what they regard a necessary overhaul of the Ukrainian military. According to their estimates, since last February Ukraine has regained control of around 150 km² of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, mostly territory that had remained in the grey zone and away from the main areas of Russian operations. Russia has presented its own counter-narrative, producing numerous materials intended to demonstrate that the areas mentioned by Zelensky remain under its control.

item.content:encoded:
For and even against: 100 days of Radev’s government in Bulgaria

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-19

16 August marked 100 days since Rumen Radev’s government was sworn in. Despite its pre-election promises, the single-party cabinet of the conservative-social Progressive Bulgaria (PB) has so far taken few steps indicating a desire to pursue fundamental domestic reforms or swiftly hold previous governments to account. On the international stage, the prime minister has criticised the EU’s foreign policy mainstream but has refrained from blocking its decisions in order to preserve Bulgaria’s image as a constructive partner. His approach to Ukraine has been the most ambiguous: Sofia has distanced itself from military and financial support for Kyiv while simultaneously seeking to strengthen bilateral cooperation.

Stability first, reforms in doubt

The Radev government’s immediate priority was to put the public finances on a more stable footing. In July, parliament passed the long-awaited budget for the remainder of the year, replacing the provisional budget that had been in place until then. The most controversial element was the deficit, which stands at 5.7% of GDP. The government has blamed its predecessors for the shortfall, alleging that they concealed or deferred some payments in order to meet the convergence criteria and join the eurozone at the beginning of 2026. item.content:encoded:
North Korean missiles strike Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia. Day 1630 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-19

Russian forces have continued their advance in the Donbas, capturing further positions south and east of the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk urban area.Humanitarian problems are worsening in both cities, with water now being delivered to Sloviansk by tanker trucks. Rai-Oleksandrivka, the last key junction east of Sloviansk, has most likely fallen entirely under Russian control. Fighting continues on the approaches to Druzhkivka from the Kostiantynivka and Pokrovsk directions, while the northern partof Kostiantynivka remainsin the grey zone. Meanwhile, Russian forces have advanced to around 3 km of Dobropillia from the south and east. The situation around Lyman remains unclear, with Ukrainian forces continuing to launch counterattacks aimed at preventing Russian troops from also outflanking the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk urban area from the north.

Russian sabotage and reconnaissance groups have entered Orikhiv from the east, and have also managed to disrupt Ukrainian defences between the town and Mala Tokmachka, which is now under attack from two directions (fighting for the settlement has continued since 2023). The relative freedom of action enjoyed by these groups suggests that Ukrainian defences in the central part of Zaporizhzhia Oblast are weakening. item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-19

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.
